name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset is a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research. The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consists of 8 languages - English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Polish. It includes about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages.
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, it, pt, pl
citeAs: @article{Pratap2020MLSAL, title={MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research}, author={Vineel Pratap and Qiantong Xu and Anuroop Sriram and Gabriel Synnaeve and Ronan Collobert}, journal={ArXiv}, year={2020}, volume={abs/2012.03411}}
rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. Audio files were downloaded using LibriVox APIs and data preparation tools from the LibriLight open source library. All audio data was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz for further processing.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from LibriVox, most of which are based on Project Gutenberg text data. LibriVox and Project Gutenberg data are released in the public domain.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions and Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss. The segmentation process involved running inference on audio to generate viterbi token sequences with timestamps, then splitting audio at silence intervals within the 10-20 second range. Numbers in text were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels. Heuristics were applied to handle hyphens and apostrophes, including removing end-of-line hyphens and filtering rare words with unusual hyphen/apostrophe usage.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text normalization was performed including NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), removal of hyphens used for end-of-line hyphenation, and filtering characters outside valid unicode ranges based on language orthography. Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Books with corrupted metadata (missing title or speaker/author information) and audiobooks with multiple speakers were removed. Candidate transcripts with WER >40% between pseudo label and matched text were filtered out.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human transcribers performed verification of development and test set transcripts. Transcribers listened to audio files while viewing the transcript and were asked to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors to avoid introducing bias. Corrections included diacritic errors, missing words, and missing apostrophes.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Trained acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss were used to generate pseudo labels. For English, a pre-trained model using TDS encoder and CTC loss on LibriSpeech was used. Beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models was performed for pseudo label generation. Smith-Waterman alignment algorithm was used for transcript retrieval with matching score of 2 and substitution/insertion/deletion score of -1. TF-IDF similarity scoring on bigrams was used for document retrieval.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of people who have donated their voice online. Gender information is included for speakers.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) training, testing, and validation. It can also be used for Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. Limited supervision datasets are provided including 10 hour sets, 1 hour sets, and six 10-minute sets for low resource training benchmarks.
